title: Poultry health and disease control
competency: Explain causes of poultry disease and how to control them.

keywords.def: Keeping new birds apart for two weeks to watch for sickness.
A disease caused by viruses, bacteria or parasites that can spread.
Giving a vaccine to protect birds from a disease.

en.text: Infectious diseases enter a flock through contaminated materials and sick birds. Do not buy birds from unknown sources during outbreaks; quarantine new birds for two weeks. Poor ventilation builds up ammonia and causes breathing problems. Diseases are infectious (viral, bacterial, parasitic) or non-infectious (feed deficiency, toxicity). Control them with hygiene, good housing, feeding, chick care, vaccination and deworming.

screens.title: New hens
screens.ask: A neighbour gives you 3 new hens. What should you do first?
opts: Keep them apart for two weeks and watch them
Put them straight in with your flock
screens.after: New birds may carry disease. Keep them apart (quarantine) for two weeks first.

screens.title: 3.4.6 Poultry health
paras: Infectious diseases enter through contaminated materials and sick birds.
Do not buy chickens from unknown sources, especially during outbreaks.
Quarantine new birds for two weeks, away from the flock.
Crowding increases the risk of cross-infection.

screens.title: Ventilation
paras: Poor ventilation builds up ammonia gas from droppings.
This causes sneezing, running eyes and mouth discharge.

screens.title: 3.4.7 Common diseases and 3.4.8 Disease control
screens.note: Prevent disease with hygiene, housing, flock structure, chick care and feeding. Also vaccinate, deworm, and treat external parasites.
